channel.title: Affil3 — buying guides
channel.description: Kitchen buying guides, checked against the maker's own specification sheet

item.title: Wireless probe or instant-read thermometer: which do you actually need?
item.description: The difference between a probe left in the food and an instant-read check, with the USDA safe minimum temperatures cited to source.

item.title: Air fryer or toaster oven: which one actually replaces the other?
item.description: How to decide whether a basket air fryer, an oven-style air fryer, or both belong on your counter.

item.title: Dual-basket air fryer: when two baskets earn the counter space
item.description: A buyer's guide to deciding whether a dual-basket air fryer fits how you cook, without claiming which product is better.

item.title: Is your meat thermometer telling you the right number?
item.description: The USDA safe minimum temperatures, where to put the probe, and the difference between an instant-read spot check and a leave-in wireless probe.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: A 26-quart countertop oven promises air frying, baking, rotisserie and more. Six questions that separate the functions you will use from the ones on the box.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: Dishwasher claims, window designs and real counter footprints: how to judge the two costs nobody puts on the box, using manufacturer specifications.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Quarts are the easiest number to misread on an air fryer listing. Here is how to compare 6, 8 and 26 quart units honestly, including what the numbers do not tell you.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: Basket and oven-style air fryers are different tools. Here is what actually changes between them, using manufacturer specifications from three units compared side by side.
